newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PROFIT-TAKING HITS ABACUS AFTER VIDEO BUY.
newsitem.headline: PROFIT-TAKING HITS ABACUS AFTER VIDEO BUY.

text.p: Shares in South African firm Abacus Technology Holdings Ltd dipped on Tuesday following the firm's announcement of its buy of National Home Video Group for 5.26 million rand, dealers said.
By 0930 GMT the firm's shares had dropped 18 cents to 250 cents in a fall that made it the fourth biggest loser of the day in percentage terms on the Johannesburg bourse.
Dealers said the drop was due to market players taking profits after a rise on the back of speculation that a deal was being done after the firm issued a cautionary announcement.
"Now everyone knows what the deal is. People are taking some profits," one dealer said.

The deal, effective retrospectively to March 1, 1997, will be settled by the allotting and issuing of 1.1 million ordinary Abacus shares at 180 cents each and 1.82 million non-voting "N" shares at 180 cents.
Abacus said the net assets acquired, excluding intangibles, amounted to some 700,000 rand.
